chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja' Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him):

"When the Day of Resurrection comes, you will be brought, O Ali, upon a noble steed of light, and upon your head will be a crown whose light has already illuminated [everything], and it will nearly blind the eyesight of the people of the gathering. Then a call will come from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is His glory — [asking]: 'Where is the vicegerent of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah?' So you will say: 'Here I am.' Then the caller will announce: 'O Ali! Admit those who love you to Paradise, and those who opposed you to the Fire. For you are the divider of Paradise, and you are the divider of the Fire.'"

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The gathering place on the Day of Resurrection where all people stand before God for judgment
key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: An expression of God's transcendent majesty, often used in hadith before quoting divine speech or decree
key_terms.خَلِيفَة: Vicegerent or successor; here used in the divine proclamation affirming Ali's status as the designated successor of the Prophet
key_terms.قَسِيم: Divider or distributor; the title 'qasim al-jannah wa al-nar' (divider of Paradise and Fire) is a specific honorific given to Imam Ali in Shia tradition
key_terms.نَجِيب: A noble riding animal (camel or horse), used here to signify Ali's elevated rank on the Day of Resurrection

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about Imam Ali's role as the divider of Paradise and Hellfire (qasim al-jannah wa al-nar) on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) eschatological proclamation to Imam Ali (AS) regarding his exalted station on the Day of Resurrection. On that day, Ali will arrive on a luminous mount wearing a blazing crown, and will be divinely called as the 'vicegerent of Muhammad,' before being given the authority to allocate people to Paradise or Hellfire based on their love or enmity toward him. The hadith was narrated by Abd Allah ibn Umar (a companion of the Prophet) and preserved in the amali (dictated sessions) of Sheikh Saduq through a chain that includes both Sunni and Shia transmitters. For the Shia audience, this narration affirmed the theological concept of Ali as qasim al-jannah wa al-nar ('divider of Paradise and Hellfire'), a title that signifies his role as the criterion of truth and the arbiter of salvation on Judgment Day.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Mu’addab narrated to us from Ahmad b. `Ali al-Isfahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi. He said: Abu Raja’ Qurayba b. Sa`id narrated to us from Hammad b. Zayd from `Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj from Nafi` from `Abdullah b. `Umar. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said to `Ali b. Abi Talib (as):

On the Day of Resurrection, you will be given – O `Ali – a garment of light, and upon your head will be a crown with an illuminating light [so bright that] it will almost put out the vision of the people of the judgment. Then, a call will come from Allah: “Where is the vicegerent of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah?” So, you will say: “I am he.” He said: So, the caller will call: “O `Ali! Take your lovers to Paradise and those who opposed you to the Fire.” You are the divider of Paradise, and you are the divider of the Fire.
